where: code/link/mmse_predict.m:79-89 (measure: R = mean(y y^H) of single-tap snapshots; MRC reference r taken at sy(1)), mmse_predict.m:25-30; code/link/validate_phy.m:66, 409, 430, 450; code/tests/test_core.m:5637 (p.tdl = false)
title: On the delay line, our own multipath echoes (ISI) are read as a separable interferer, which raises false nulling flags on clean high-Eb/N0 links
fix:
Leave mmse_predict.m and C1p unchanged. Close the coverage gap instead:
1. In validate_phy.m v13, add a clean row with our own signal on the delay line, using the pools' draws: p.tdl=true, tdl_random, k_random and corr_random true, rx_combiner 'mrc', Eb/N0 15 dB, at least 100 flights x 11 frames, n_rx of the profile. Rules: |median G| <= 1 dB and Q(c,10), the share of G >= C.rule_mmse_db, at most 2%. Measured now: 0.36% for n_rx 3 and 0.86% for n_rx 4, so both rules pass.
2. Report the corners K -5 dB / 1000 ns and K 0 dB / 300 ns as informational rows. They read +2.8 and +2.2 dB, and the deployed MMSE improves BER there.
3. Add one delay-line clean case to test_mmse_predict_known_symbols (test_core.m:5637). Fixed corners would fail the 1.5 dB clean-median check, so use pool draws.
4. In the mmse_predict.m header, say in one line that G also counts the single-tap suppression of our own echoes at whole-symbol lags, a few dB on low-K, long-spread links.
5. Keep the sel-08 threshold chosen on validation frames that already run the delay line.

Only if the new row fails should own-lag covariance subtraction be tuned on dev frames.
evidence: Every pool flight runs the delay line (init_params tdl=true; K drawn U(-5,20) dB; delay_spread.m log-normal with median 234-372 ns, clipped at 2.25 us). Our own ISI at whole-symbol lags has a spatial structure (each diffuse tap differs per antenna), so it ends up in R. The single-tap DMI partly nulls it, while the single-tap MRC at sy(1) stays ISI-limited. The deployed receivers do not suffer this ISI: the MRC receiver runs MRC over the antennas and the rx_taps lags plus a linear MMSE equalizer (build_threat_model.m:145-146, rx_taps.m), and the MMSE configuration uses space-time taps. Switching to nulling therefore gains nothing from this ISI, but G credits it. Reproduction used private copies of mmse_predict.m, frame_layout.m and tdl_profile.m (same frame, RRC, tdl_profile taps, arrival at the LoS, perfect frequency; scripts in scratchpad rev88/phy/syn_test.m and syn_pool.m). Flat clean link: G median -0.5 to -1.5 dB, p99 <= +0.3 dB, 0% >= 6 dB. This matches V13's -0.6 dB, so the flat channel is fine. Clean delay-line frames over the pools' draws (K U(-5,20), delay_spread.m bands, rho U(0.3,0.9), 400 flights per point): at Eb/N0 15 dB, G p99 is +8.6 dB with n_rx 3 and +10.2 dB with n_rx 4; the share >= 6 dB is 5.5% / 8.5% and the share >= 3 dB is 24% / 25%. Among K < 5 dB the share >= 6 dB is 12% / 19%. At Eb/N0 6 dB it is 0% / 0.5%. Fixed cases at 15 dB: ds 300 ns, K 0 dB: 10.7%; ds 1000 ns, K -5 dB: 14% (n_rx 4: 22.7%). Effects: the rule adds spatial_diversity for antenna_fault / airframe_shadowing (rule_based_policy.m:74) and for degraded none/unknown frames (:92) on clean dispersive flights; the DQN state row mixes dispersion with interference; and sel-08's mu+3 sigma on clean validation frames would push the threshold up, losing sensitivity to real interferers. V13 cannot see any of this, for four reasons: validate_phy sets p0.tdl=false (:66); the clean row has ds 0 (:409); the V12c rows put the spread on the interferer only (p.tdl_ds_ns = [0 ds], :430); and v13_theory keeps our own ISI in Rn, so it agrees with the predictor. Rule (a) also checks only the clean median (:450), not Q(c,10), the share >= threshold. test_mmse_predict_known_symbols is flat as well. C1p bakes F.mmse_pred into about 1M simulations per profile, so this has to be settled before C1p.

where: code/link/mmse_predict.m:58-66 (line 64: if sc > 2 * sm, sm = sc; ...)
title: The arrival search keeps the first candidate that doubles the running best, not the highest-SINR arrival
fix:
Use the fix as proposed, in code/link/mmse_predict.m:58-66. Before the loop set `s0 = sm; bm = -Inf;`. In the loop, `if sc > bm, bm = sc; bd = d; bf = dfc; bw = wc; end`. After the loop, `if bm > 2 * s0, sm = bm; D.arrival(f) = bd; D.df_hz(f) = bf; D.w_mmse(:, :, f) = bw; end`. Keeping `bm = -Inf` means `bd` and the other values are never read when every candidate is skipped. The acceptance set is unchanged, so the code then matches the header, d88 doc lines 103-106 and the st_sync max.

Also add a synthetic test with fractional arrival, receiver's arrival 2 symbols off: D.arrival must be the candidate of the highest SINR. This guards against a regression, because V13 measures its theory at D.arrival and cannot see it.

Re-running mmse_pred is cheap. It is computed when the pools are built after C1p, and the plan already rebuilds them, so no extra rerun is needed if the fix lands before C1p.
evidence: The header (lines 26-30) and docs/d88_blockers.md describe the search as finding the arrival of the highest MMSE SINR, taken when it reaches 2x the receiver's arrival. The code compares each candidate with the running best (sm is updated in place), so a candidate scanned before the true arrival (e.g. a quarter-symbol neighbour) can block it. Test: synthetic clean flat link, n_rx 3, receiver's arrival 2 symbols off (scratchpad rev88/phy/syn_greedy.m, 200 frames per point). The true arrival was found in 56/200 frames at Eb/N0 -3 dB and 146/200 at 0 dB; a max-then-compare search found it in 200/200. G under-read by a median 1.8 dB, at most 3.0 dB, at -3 dB; there was no effect at 6 and 15 dB. The search runs only where MMSE SINR < 0 dB, i.e. frames the MRC receiver loses under strong jammers. Those are the low-SINR frames near the threshold (d88 doc: at 30 dB, 5-33% of frames read below 6 dB).

title: KPI 7 latency does not time the new per-frame MMSE predictor, which takes 9-20 ms when the arrival search runs
fix:
1) Time the predictor in LAT (measure_latency.m section 1 and line 100):
- For each run, keep the all-antenna samples as the combiner sees them: out.get('Rx_IQ') (raw, before the Cal_db scaling), and sy = reshape(out.get('Rx_S'), 8, []).
- Store each frame as x.iqa = iqa(:,:,max(1,k-1):k) and x.sy = sy(1:2, max(1,k-1):k). When k > 1, set x.sy(:,1) = NaN, so frame k-1 only provides filter memory and is not measured; otherwise the cost doubles.
- Inside the features timer, call g = mmse_predict(x.iqa, p0, x.sy); obs.mmse_pred = g(end).
- I verified that this gives the same G as the full-run value on all 80 LAT frames.
- Add the predictor's own column to names/tm, and keep the jamming run: it is where the search fires (18/20 frames).

2) Make the arrival search cheap (mmse_predict.m:58-66):
- Score the 16 candidates with a cheap statistic and no residual_frequency, for example the DMI SINR on the long training alone, or measure() without the frequency step.
- Run residual_frequency + measure only at the best candidate (or the best 2), keeping the 2x acceptance rule.
- Then rerun validate_phy('V13') and test_mmse_predict_known_symbols to confirm G is unchanged within tolerance, especially the 30 dB jam and tone rows, which depend on the search and the frequency correction.
- Optionally run mmse_predict with maxNumCompThreads(1): it works on 3x3 matrices, and in my run 8 threads were about 2x slower than 1 core.
- Rerun LAT after both changes, before the KPI 7 verdict is read.
evidence: LAT times the spectrogram, link_features (which reads the precomputed M), the detector and the policies. obs.mmse_pred is copied from x.M, which extract_closed_loop_frames computed outside the timers. Unlike the old mmse_gain (read from the receiver's own estimator outputs 4-5), mmse_predict is not demodulation work. It is an extra decision input computed from the raw all-antenna IQ: RRC filtering, MMSE-weighted frequency estimation, and a held-out DMI over 12 groups. With the arrival search it repeats this for 16 more candidates. Measured on one frame on this machine (scratchpad rev88/phy/syn_time.m). Without the search: 0.99 ms median (1 core), 1.55 ms (8 threads). With the search: 9.24 ms median / 12.4 ms p95 (1 core) and 20.3 ms median / 26.6 ms p95 (8 threads). KPI 7 requires a median < 10 ms and p95 < 20 ms (measure_all_kpis.m:343), and the search fires exactly on strongly jammed frames.

title: B1 accepts spectrograms built from an unrepaired 2N dataset, so skipping A6 silently brings the scrambled feature 13 back
fix:
Make the change in two places, and cover both sets.

1. In extract_spectrograms.m, between :77 and the save at :78, add:
`spec.meta.frames_checked = true;`
Optionally also record the dataset's identity: `spec.meta.src_align = isfield(ds, 'align_gcs');`

2. In prepare_data.m, after :25 (main path) and after :86 (prepare_fresh_test), add:
`assert(isfield(sp0, 'meta') && isfield(sp0.meta, 'frames_checked') && sp0.meta.frames_checked, 'prepare_data:stale', '%s was not built by the guarded A6 (run repair_align, then extract_spectrograms)', <file>)`
On the fresh path, `<file>` is `['data/spectrograms_fresh' sfx '.mat']`.

Two optional extras:
- B1 could also refuse a spectrograms file older than its dataset (`dir(f_in).datenum > dir(f_spec).datenum`), which follows the datenum style already used in eval_unseen_snr.m:268.
- Add a test_core source check that the stamp is written in A6 and required in both B1 paths.
evidence: The 2N signature only exists in the dataset, and only A6 checks it (extract_spectrograms.m:28-29). Spectrograms built from a 2N dataset still hold N rows in every field, because A6 read meas.align(idx) with idx 1..N. So the new B1 guard (assert_frames(sp0, numel(sp0.run), ...)) passes on them. The profile 1 files show this state right now: data/dataset.mat was repaired at 13:59 and dataset_fresh.mat at 14:03 today, but spectrograms.mat (02:21) and spectrograms_fresh.mat (07:35) are still the scrambled ones. Running run_stage('B1') or the fresh B1 before A6 rebuilds splits.mat and splits_fresh.mat from the scrambled column. The norm asserts in eval_detector.m:33/37, compare_architectures.m:44 and eval_ood_detection.m:64 then pass too, because both files are equally stale. Nothing downstream would stop the retrain on the old input.

where: code/link/mmse_predict.m:55-58 and 123-147 (residual_frequency); code/link/validate_phy.m:289 (ok leaves out r13) and 450 (clean-row rule); redeploy plan for profile 3
title: Profile 3 (4 antennas): mmse_pred fails V13 (9/11), and nothing in the plan runs V13 or stops on it before p3's C1p
fix:
1. mmse_predict.m:58-66: resolve the pilot ambiguity inside the existing search.
   - In frames where sm < 1 (the same gate as the arrival search; every under-read frame had a measured MMSE SINR below -9 dB), also evaluate the frequency hypotheses sy(2,f) + m*fp, with fp = p.symbol_rate/(p.pilot_block + p.pilot_every) and m = -3..3 (m = +3 was needed).
   - Keep the largest held-out MMSE SINR under the same 2x (3 dB) acceptance, and store the chosen df.
   - Checked: on p3 under pool conditions this gives 99% >= 6 dB at tone 30 dB against the deployed MMSE receiver's 95% BER < 1e-2. On the V13 tone-30 row it gives 100%.
   - Alternative: take the frequency from the MMSE receiver's own acquisition (st_sync on the delay line).
2. validate_phy.m:391-449, V13.
   - Its tone rows run p.tdl=false, but both profiles deploy p.tdl=true. On flat, the deployed MMSE receiver aliases too (BER 0.5). So run the tone rows on the delay line as deployed, or add a column for the deployed MMSE receiver's measured SINR or BER on the same seeds. Judge G against what that receiver achieves, not only against the perfect-sync optimum. Do not tune the predictor until the flat row passes.
   - Make the clean-row rule (validate_phy.m:450) relative to the predictor's own combiners' theory (|G - Q(1,2)| <= 1 dB) or allow the RMB loss 10log10((K+2-M)/(K+1)) for K=16 (-0.84 dB at M=4).
3. Before C1p in p1 and p3, run validate_phy('V13'): about 11 min on p3 on this loaded machine.
4. Have result_status/measure_all_kpis read results/phy_validation_v13.txt (params_id check), or fold r13.pass into ok at validate_phy.m:289, so the verdict reaches the report.
evidence: I ran validate_phy('V13') at 725a2f1 in a private copy with uav-gcs-v7-p3/params.mat and profile.json (n_rx 4, params_id 7ecc49e9...). Result: 'V13 predicted MMSE gain: 9/11 rows -> FAIL' (7.9 min). Tone 30 dB: G +6.7 dB, against +0.0 for its own combiners and +26.3 for the optimum. MMSE meas -11.0 dB, 54% of frames >= 6 dB. The clean link reads -1.0 dB (its own combiners' theory -0.9), so it fails the fixed 1 dB rule. The same check on profile 1's live params (add18af2..., n_rx 3) passes 11/11 (tone 30 dB +23.7). A per-frame diagnostic of the tone-30 row on p3 shows the cause. The MRC receiver's cfo_hz jumps by 12-22 kHz between frames of one run (seed 1 -12.8/-34.6 kHz; seed 2 -80/-97 kHz; seed 3 -86/-98 kHz). D.df_hz then sits at +5 to +9.2 kHz, the edge of residual_frequency's unambiguous range: pilots every 52 symbols at 1 Msym/s gives +/-9.6 kHz. Only the frames whose cfo is near the true value read G about +28 dB with MMSE about +10 dB. The arrival search covers time only, never frequency. The tone at 23 and 30 dB is a pool cell (decision_config.m:77), so p3's pools would carry the collapse that D88 set out to remove, in both the rule's nulling flag and the agent's state. V13 never reaches the record: A4v is not in the redo list, and both profiles' results/phy_validation.txt (written at c2c8b8b) hold no V13 line. validate_phy's ok at :289 leaves r13 out, so p2's in-chain A4v would not stop on it either. KPI/result_status read only phy_validation.txt.

1. edge_map.m:604: add `CK.maha_thr = PP.maha_thr;` before link_env('tables', CK, ...) at :605. The threshold is applied at decision time, so the check pools need no rebuild. Copy rule_mmse_db the same way once the agent stores it.
2. v3d_engine.m:43: add 'maha_thr' to the load list, then set `if isfield(Q,'maha_thr'), PP.maha_thr = Q.maha_thr; end` before link_env('tables', PP) at :47.
3. demo_gui.m:63: load 'maha_thr' too. At :102 use Q.maha_thr when it is present (fall back to Tood.maha), and set the slider default at :201 to the agent's retention. Two ways to get it: have train_dqn save unk_retain next to maha_thr, or compute it as 100*mean(env.maha_val >= Q.maha_thr) and round it to the slider's range.

evidence: edge_map sets PP.maha_thr = Q.maha_thr (:123). The off-grid check pools then take only confirm, alarm_mode and drop_db from PP (:604), so policy_run_set runs CK with CK.maha_thr = T.maha from C1c. demo_gui builds PP.maha_thr from ood_thresholds(0.95) (:102) and never loads Q.maha_thr. v3d_engine uses the pools' PP.maha_thr. title: B3a report does not say which column is the deployed monitor's class; its 'fused+latch (OOF)' column is not fully out of fold
fix:
**1. State the deployed monitor in the report.**
- In the `if fz` block, set `latch_on = onset_shape('on', FZ.FM);`.
- Print `deployed monitor: fused class (FM.latch = false)` or `... fused+latch (FM.latch = true)` in the validation header and above the test fused table.
- When latch_on is false, title the latch columns 'fused+latch (not deployed)'. This also matches latch_runs.m:6.

**2. Make the latched validation column truly out of fold, as select_fusion.m:89-111 does.**
- Before the variant loop, compute og, oy and orun from sp.val.gain_ant and yv_cyc using onset_shape('events', ..., j0, decision_config().heal). They do not depend on the variant, so this runs once.
- Compute the per-fold thresholds: `ko = fold_of_run(ismember-index of orun in runs)` and `tf(k) = onset_shape('choose', og(ko~=k), oy(ko~=k))`.
- Pass tf to fused_oof. Latch each fold separately: `pl(fold==k,:) = latch_runs(pc(fold==k,:), va.run(fold==k), va.pos(fold==k), va.gain_ant(fold==k,:), classes, tf(k))`.
- Keep FM.os_thr only for the test-set reading at :129, labelled 'deployed threshold'.

If you prefer not to refit, relabel the column at :139 as 'fused+latch (deployed os_thr, in-sample)'.
evidence: The report prints both 'fused' and 'fused+latch' with a generic note (:147). It never records FM.latch (false on both profiles' validation, d87), so a reader cannot tell which column is the system's class. fused_oof refits the fusion per fold but latches with os_thr = FM.os_thr (:52, :125, :191), which was chosen on all validation sub-runs. select_fusion's val_latch_oof uses fold-wise onset_shape('choose') thresholds. So the column labelled out of fold carries a small in-sample choice.
